How to read this
Device reachability and KDS temperature are measured values. A room is Abnormal only when a KDS reading is at or above 49°C, a display/AVoIP device is unreachable, or the camera is offline — lighting never triggers an Abnormal verdict, it is reported for information only. Only the displays Danny declared are monitored (SM-11-01 = 4 LED TV, SM-11-02 = 2, SM-11-03..06 = 1 LED wall each, SM-11-07 = 2, SM-11-08 = 2); every other bright region in a frame is a traditional whiteboard and is ignored — except a region whose OCR reads an AVoIP standby banner, which is one of the room’s TVs. In a dual / quad room all displays share one source, so if one of them is idle / on standby while another shows live content the room is out of sync and counts as Abnormal — but only after the same mismatch is seen on two consecutive runs; a first occurrence is marked OUT OF SYNC (1ST RUN) and is not yet abnormal. "Sync not verified" means too few displays could be isolated in the frame, so check by eye. A device counts as unreachable only on an explicit fail; unknown means the poller has not reached it yet and is never a fault. Pixel-level correlation between displays is unreliable at these viewing angles and is therefore not used for the verdict. Display screen state comes from OCR plus pixel behaviour of each camera frame: Idle is deliberately narrow — only the AVoIP decoder standby banner, the Windows lock screen (clock only) and an all-blank screen. A Windows desktop or an application that simply sits static for a long time is reported as Content on screen, not Idle. Picture-sync between displays still has to be confirmed by eye — open the attached AV_room_audit.html, where each room’s live frame sits inside its TV / LED wall cell. Person count is not available; the “Use” column is the share of pixels that changed over 12 seconds.

Attachments: AV_room_audit.html (full report, snapshot inside each TV / LED wall cell) · all_rooms_*.jpg (3x3 contact sheet).
